spec.name: sandwich-key-mix-v1
spec.limitations: Per-byte, 8-bit key: no cross-byte diffusion, so equal plaintext bytes give equal ciphertext bytes at every offset, and a single known plaintext/ciphertext byte pair lets an attacker scan all 256 keys. Because add_key sits in the middle, the inverse's inner move is add(256-k), a secret-dependent subtraction the op set cannot express; decryption needs a host-side 256-k, so the inverse is not itself a program here. The three key touches (xor, add, xor separated by rotations) do not raise entropy past 256 keys and give no extra state. The map is easily tabulated: 256 chosen plaintext bytes reveal the entire permutation, after which the key follows from the known final xor. Treat as a toy keyed byte permutation, not a cipher.
spec.math: With k the secret byte: x1 = x xor k, x2 = rol2(x1), x3 = x2 + k (mod 256), x4 = x3 xor 198, x5 = rol4(x4), x6 = x5 + 33 (mod 256), y = x6 xor k. Each step is a bijection on the 256-byte set: xor with a constant is an involution, addition mod 256 is a permutation with inverse add(256-c), and rol n permutes the 8 bit positions with inverse rol((8-n) mod 8), so rol2/rol6 and rol4/rol4 are inverse pairs. A composition of bijections is a bijection, hence exactly invertible for every k. Inversion runs reversed ops with reversed arguments: y -> xor k -> add 223 (= -33) -> rol 4 -> xor 198 -> add (256-k) -> rol 6 -> xor k, recovering x; only the add(256-k) step lies outside the op set.
spec.assumptions: The key k is a fixed secret byte chosen uniformly and reused for every input byte; ops apply independently per byte with rol wrapping inside 8 bits (n reduced mod 8); all other operands are public constants; decryption is performed by a host able to compute 256-k; no nonce, IV, or chaining is assumed; *_key operands are ignored.
